books.section: Topic 4.3 Politics and Regional Interests, B. The American System and Sectionalism
Henry Clay and the American System

stimulus.text:
| Part of the plan | What it would do |
|---|---|---|
| Protective tariff | Tax imported goods so American-made goods cost less |
| Second Bank of the United States | Steady the currency and lend credit for business |
| Internal improvements | Build roads and canals to link the regions |

Henry Clay of Kentucky called the three parts his American System. Congress chartered the Second Bank and passed a protective tariff in 1816.

stem: Clay’s American System most closely continued the economic program of

options.text: Alexander Hamilton, who also favored a national bank, tariffs, and aid to manufacturing
Thomas Jefferson, who opposed a national bank and high tariffs
options.misconception: Jefferson opposed the Bank and protective tariffs; the System copies the program he fought.

options.text: Andrew Jackson, who vetoed the Bank’s recharter and opposed federal internal improvements
options.misconception: Jackson fought the System’s Bank and its federal spending; he is its opponent, not its model.

options.text: the Hartford Convention delegates, who opposed federal power
options.misconception: The Hartford delegates wanted to limit federal power; the System expands it.

rationales.A: Hamilton’s program was a national bank, tariffs to aid manufacturing, and federal support for commerce. Clay’s three parts are the same program under a new name.
rationales.B: Jefferson opposed a national bank and high tariffs, and cut federal spending. The American System is the program Jefferson argued against.
rationales.C: Jackson vetoed the Bank’s recharter in 1832 and opposed federal internal improvements. He spent his presidency dismantling Clay’s program, not continuing it.
rationales.D: The Hartford delegates met to limit federal power over New England’s trade. The American System uses federal power; it does not limit it.
rationales.general:
1. List Clay’s parts. A tariff, a national bank, and federal aid to roads and canals.
2. Ask who proposed that mix first. Hamilton proposed a bank, tariffs, and federal aid to manufacturing in the 1790s.
3. Check the others. Jefferson and Jackson opposed the Bank; Hartford wanted federal power limited.
4. Put it together. Clay restated Hamilton’s program for a new generation.
Background: the books note the marked continuity between Hamilton’s program and Clay’s American System, including tariffs, a central bank, and aid to manufacturing.
Remember: when a plan has three familiar parts, match the whole set, not one piece.
